content: The puddle sign is a clinical maneuver utilized during physical examination in the field of gastroenterology to identify the presence of ascites. This technique is particularly effective in detecting small volumes of ascitic fluid, as little as 120 mL, whereas other methods such as shifting dullness and bulging flanks typically require a minimum of 500 mL of fluid to be detected. When compared to auscultatory percussion, the puddle sign demonstrates greater specificity but lower sensitivity.
